saints.name: St. Florian
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A Roman officer in Noricum who confessed Christ and was drowned in the Enns during Diocletian's persecution…
biography: Born about 250, Florian rose to high office in the Roman administration of Noricum, in what is now Upper Austria, and dwelt at Aelium Cetium, the modern St. Pölten. When Diocletian's persecution reached the province and the governor Aquilinus imprisoned some forty Christians at Lauriacum, Florian hastened thither to stand with them.

Seized by his former comrades, he professed the faith openly and refused to sacrifice; he was scourged, his shoulders flayed, and condemned to the water. On 4 May 304 a millstone was hung about his neck and he was drowned in the river Enns below Lauriacum, the Lorch of today.

A matron named Valeria is said to have buried his body where the abbey of St. Florian stands near Linz. In the twelfth century portions of his relics were carried to Poland, and he is honored as a patron of that land and of Upper Austria. Because legend tells that he once saved a burning house with one pitcher of water, he is invoked against fire, the patron of firefighters.
saints.knownFor: His steadfast confession under Diocletian and his patronage of firefighters.
